idea: Full factorial design over several scenario factors (e.g. demand level x signal timing method x bus priority on/off) with seeds as replicates: ANOVA table splitting main effects, two- and three-factor interactions (Examples J 3x3x3, K 2x3x2x2, L 3x2x2, N 2^3 with replicates and judges), orthogonal polynomial linear/quadratic contrasts for ordered levels (Ex J, M: coefficients -3,-1,1,3), log transform of the response when effects are multiplicative, and pooling of insignificant interactions into the error. Tells which design factors matter and whether they interact, which one-factor-at-a-time run_experiment cannot.
does: Builds a factorial grid of scenarios, runs seeds, returns ANOVA with contrasts and interaction data
inputs: factors with levels (edit/scale/extension), seeds, response KPI, transform
outputs: ANOVA table (SS, df, F, p) per effect, linear/quadratic contrasts, fitted cell means, best cell
cite: Examples J, K, L, M, N
notes: Orthogonal contrast coding makes it a regression; reuse regress. Unbalanced cells (Ex O) handled by sequential model comparison of residual SS.

idea: Nested (hierarchical) ANOVA with random effects (Ex Q yarns/bobbins/lengths; Ex S setting stations/regulators): split the variance of a KPI into between-seed (replication) and within-run (time-interval) components to estimate the sampling variance of a scenario mean and the number of seeds or minutes needed for a target CI half-width; detect anomalous units by residuals (regulator J2).
does: Nested ANOVA variance components for a KPI across seeds, intervals and roads, with sample-size advice
outputs: variance components, ICC, seeds needed, outlier units
notes: ACMS has MSER and CIs but no budget planner for how many seeds to run.

idea: Plot log(group s.d.) against log(group mean) across scenario cells and use the slope to pick the transform (slope 1 -> log; 0.5 -> sqrt; 0 -> none), Box-Cox style (Ex Q slope 0.62 vs 3.39 flagged a problem); apply before ANOVA or t-tests on delays and queues.
does: Suggests power transform from the sd-vs-mean relation

idea: Chi-square homogeneity test of k estimates with standard errors: X2 = sum (y_i - ybar_w)^2 / v_i, df k-1, ybar_w the inverse-variance weighted mean (Ex C). Use to check whether a treatment effect is the same across seeds, demand levels, or road classes before pooling, and to pool consistent estimates with inverse-variance weights.
does: Cochran Q-style test and pooled estimate
notes: Also pools effects across experiments run at different times.

idea: ML fit of a gamma distribution (mean mu, shape beta) per unit to intervals (Ex T: air-conditioner failure intervals, shape 0.46 for one aircraft indicates clustering) with a likelihood-difference test that the shape is common to all units; apply to headways at each detector or origin: shape<1 bunching, =1 Poisson, >1 regular. Richer than the index of dispersion.
does: Gamma/Weibull/lognormal fit and common-shape test for headways or inter-arrival times
inputs: run id, road or origin end
notes: Ex B shows lognormal intervals; geometric mean as summary.

idea: Logistic regression with deviance goodness-of-fit and standardised residuals (Ex H fault occurrence on process and purity, Ex M proportion graded, Ex X college plans, Ex V case-control odds ratios): model a binary per-vehicle or per-bus outcome (stopped at signal, delayed over threshold, gap rejected, TSP granted) on covariates; stepwise entry; log-linear models for categorical tables (Ex W).
does: Binary logistic regression by Newton-Raphson with odds ratios and fit statistics
inputs: binary outcome and covariates from run data
outputs: coefficients, odds ratios, SE, deviance, predicted probabilities
cite: Examples H, L, M, V, X
notes: Book warns standard errors understate when outcomes within a batch correlate (Ex M).

idea: Single-linkage hierarchical clustering and classical metric multidimensional scaling (largest eigenvalues of the centred distance matrix) from a pairwise similarity (Set 14): cluster roads or OD pairs by similarity of their series, and plot scenarios in 2D from a KPI distance matrix.
does: Hierarchical clustering and MDS coordinates from a similarity matrix
notes: Needs an eigen solver (shared with kpi_pca).

idea: Compare two processes applied in alternating order under a drifting background (Ex F): regress response on process indicator plus linear and quadratic orthogonal polynomials in time; estimate the process effect after removing trend. In ACMS: compare two signal plans or agents alternating inside one long run through the daily demand curve.
does: Process effect with polynomial time trend and standard error

idea: When many scenarios cannot all be run with every seed, use incomplete blocks (seeds as blocks of 2 to 3 scenarios) and the within-block analysis (Ex I: differences within blocks, treatment effects with equal SE) to compare all scenarios at lower cost.
does: Assigns scenarios to seed blocks and estimates effects from within-block differences
notes: Runs are cheap headless, so full design is usually fine; low priority.
